query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: High-throughput molecular dynamics simulations combined with machine learning models can accurately and efficiently predict the melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in their crystalline or as-cast/homogenized single-phase state.
generation.intervention: Perform high-throughput MD simulations to generate thermodynamic data and train ML models on these results to predict phase transformation properties.
generation.conditions: Simulations and experiments conducted under ambient or standard pressure with controlled temperature ramps that minimize kinetic effects; measurements taken under inert or reducing atmospheres as appropriate.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic-scale disorder and chemical interactions that govern local structural configurations and phase transitions.
generation.mechanism: MD simulations capture the detailed atomic interactions and free-energy changes during melting, while ML models generalize these relationships to predict properties for new HEA compositions; this integrated approach bridges nanoscale structural mediators to macroscopic thermodynamic properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Predictions of melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, and volume change at melting should agree with experimental results within approximately ±10% relative accuracy (or within ±50 K for melting temperature), with similar performance for key liquid-phase properties.
generation.baseline: Traditional empirical correlations, isolated calorimetric measurements, or standard CALPHAD methods that do not account for atomic-scale disorder.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to apply primarily to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys under ambient pressure, with reduced reliability for off-stoichiometric compositions or extreme thermodynamic conditions.
generation.uncertainty: There remains uncertainty in extending the method to compositions or pressure regimes not well represented in the training dataset, and in fully capturing complex multi-element interactions beyond the calibrated range.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of equiatomic and near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys. Perform differential scanning calorimetry, in-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction, and calorimetric liquid-phase measurements to independently determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy/entropy, and volume changes at melting. Compare these values to predictions from the MD-ML approach.
measurements: Differential scanning calorimetry for melting temperature and latent heat
In-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction to assess volume expansion
Calorimetric measurements of liquid-phase thermodynamic properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the computational predictions deviate from the experimental measurements by more than ±50 K for melting temperature or more than ±10% for fusion enthalpy, entropy, or liquid-phase properties in multiple HEA systems, the proposed approach will be considered falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A multiscale computational approach combining ab initio molecular dynamics with machine‐learned interatomic potentials, calibrated to DFT and limited experimental data, can accurately and efficiently predict the melting point, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties for equiatomic high‐entropy alloys.
drafts.material_initial_state: Equiatomic high-entropy alloys in their crystalline state, exhibiting substantial chemical disorder.
drafts.intervention: Apply a simulation protocol that integrates molecular dynamics with thermodynamic integration techniques using machine-learned potentials specifically trained on ab initio data, to simulate the phase transformation from the crystalline alloy to the liquid phase.
drafts.conditions: Simulations run under ambient pressure with a controlled temperature ramp (i.e. heating rates that minimize kinetic undercooling) and periodic boundary conditions; calibration performed against DFT data at zero pressure.
drafts.structural_mediator: Local chemical disorder and short-range ordering in the multi-principal element system mediate the onset of melting and the associated volume expansion and latent heat phenomena.
drafts.mechanism: The strategy leverages the ability of ML potentials to capture detailed atomic interactions in a disordered alloy, while thermodynamic integration quantifies the changes in free energy as the system undergoes melting. This combined approach allows extraction of not only the melting temperature but also enthalpy, entropy, and volume changes at melting, as well as other liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Predicted melting temperatures are expected to be within ±50 K of experimental values, with similar relative accuracy (~±10%) for fusion enthalpy and entropy. Liquid-phase properties (such as heat capacity) should show comparable quantitative agreement with available experimental data.
drafts.baseline: Standard CALPHAD assessments and empirical correlations based on bulk properties, which generally offer less precise predictions and lack the capability to capture nanoscale structural mediators.
drafts.boundary: The approach is anticipated to work reliably for equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys under ambient pressure. Its applicability may be limited for off-stoichiometry systems or under extreme pressure conditions unless additional calibration is performed.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a series of experiments on a set of equiatomic high-entropy alloys where differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), in-situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction (XRD), and calorimetric liquid-phase measurements are used to independently determine melting temperature, melting enthalpy, volume change at melting, and heat capacity in the liquid phase. Parallel computational studies using the ML MD approach will predict these values.
measurements: DSC measurements of melting temperature and latent heat
In-situ high-temperature XRD to measure volume expansion at melting
Calorimetric determination of liquid-phase heat capacity and related thermodynamic properties

drafts.hypothesis: An integrated CALPHAD–machine-learning approach can predict melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and other high-temperature properties of high-entropy alloys with 5–10% accuracy across a broad range of compositions by combining atomic-scale mixing entropy considerations with empirical calibration from sparse experimental data.
drafts.material_initial_state: As-cast or homogenized single-phase or predominantly single-phase high-entropy alloys
drafts.intervention: Develop and train a machine-learning model on published thermochemical data for high-entropy alloys; refine the predictions by coupling with thermodynamic calculations (e.g., CALPHAD) and selectively validating with a limited set of new experimental measurements.
drafts.conditions: Elevated temperatures spanning pre-melting to above the melting range (e.g., 800–2000 K), inert or reducing atmosphere, standard pressure
drafts.structural_mediator: Complex multi-element lattice distortions that modify free energy and influence phase equilibria
drafts.mechanism: A synergy of data-driven machine learning models (trained with known thermodynamic data) and physically grounded CALPHAD calculations can capture the role of configurational entropy and chemical interactions in determining high-temperature behavior of multi-principal-element alloys.
drafts.predicted_outcome: A computationally efficient procedure that achieves melting temperature predictions within ~30 K, enthalpy and entropy of fusion within 10%, and volume changes at melting within 5%. drafts.baseline: Isolated DSC, DTA, or calorimetry measurements for single-composition or narrowly bounded multicomponent alloys, requiring extensive experimental resources for each new composition
